questions.q: What is an aggregate fact table?
options: A rollup of a base fact table to a lower dimensionality and/or higher granularity, built to accelerate query performance
A dimension table that stores only aggregated flags
A fact table with no dimension keys at all
A temporary staging table deleted at the end of every ETL run
questions.explain: Its whole purpose is to pre-compute a commonly-queried summary once, in a much smaller table, instead of scanning and summing the full detailed fact table every time.

questions.q: Why isn't the detailed fact table's grain (from Chapter 1) simply abandoned in favor of the aggregate table?
options: The detailed grain is still correct and necessary for detailed analysis — the aggregate table is an additional, faster path for commonly-asked summary questions, not a replacement
Fabric Warehouse does not allow more than one fact table per warehouse
Aggregate tables always contain more rows than the detailed fact table
The detailed fact table becomes read-only once an aggregate table exists
questions.explain: Correct, detailed grain and fast, pre-summarized grain solve different problems — the aggregate table sits alongside the detail, not instead of it.

questions.q: What T-SQL technique is used to build an aggregate table in Fabric Warehouse?
options: CREATE TABLE AS SELECT (CTAS), grouping the detailed fact by the dimension keys the aggregate needs and summing its measures
DROP TABLE, followed by manually retyping every row
A DAX measure written directly against the warehouse
ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN on the detailed fact table
questions.explain: CTAS lets you create a new, smaller table directly from a GROUP BY query against the detailed fact table — this is the real technique Microsoft's own Fabric Warehouse tutorials use.

questions.q: What is the real maintenance cost of adding an aggregate table to a warehouse?
options: It must be refreshed on a schedule to stay in sync with the detailed fact table, or reports against it will disagree with reports against the detail
There is no cost — aggregate tables update themselves automatically with zero ETL involvement
It permanently locks the detailed fact table from being queried
It requires deleting the detailed fact table entirely
questions.explain: An aggregate table is duplicated, summarized data — every time the detail gets new rows, the aggregate needs a scheduled refresh as part of the ETL orchestration, or it goes stale.

questions.q: According to Microsoft's guidance, what is an alternative way to get an aggregate-table-like performance benefit without necessarily building a separate physical warehouse table?
options: A Power BI semantic model can generate user-defined aggregations, or query the warehouse's aggregate fact table via DirectQuery
Deleting the detailed fact table so only summary data remains
Running every report query twice and averaging the results
Aggregate tables have no alternative — a physical table is always required
questions.explain: User-defined aggregations in the semantic model layer can achieve a similar effect, though that's a semantic-model decision outside this course's warehouse-focused scope.
